text:
Maya (Support): FYI - Videx (prod) reporting a spike of 504s on streaming /v1/generate since ~09:10 UTC. They say their SDK is retrying and they're getting double charges. Need triage and a short customer-facing statement.

Maya (Support): Minimal repro they sent (sanitized):
```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-stream-2","stream":true,"input":"summarize: ..."}'
```

Maya (Support): Example request_id: req_20260317_09:12:21:VIDEX: a1b2c3d4  -- saw 504 gateway + client retry loop in customer logs.

Sam (SRE): Looking. Can you drop the full request IDs + approximate client timestamps? I want to grep edge logs (gw01/gw02).

Maya (Support): Pasted three IDs from customer: req_20260317_09:12:21: a1b2c3d4, req_20260317_09:12:24: e5f6g7h8, req_20260317_09:12:31: i9j0k1l2. Customer is in us-west1 region.

Sam (SRE): I see matching entries on gw01 around 09:12:21-09:12:32. Gateway returned 504 with upstream error: "upstream read timeout" and then connection reset from runtime pool. Also a bunch of long-lived streaming connections hitting keepalive timeouts.

Leo (Eng-runtime): Can you paste the runtime logs (runtime-ppool-3) for those request_ids? I want to know if the runtime returned 502/504 or if the proxy timed out waiting for tokens. Also suspicious: kernel OOM/eviction events in same window.

Maya (Support): Customer attached partial runtime snippet: "2026-03-17T09:12:21Z runtime-ppool-3 INFO request a1b2c3d4 processing chunk 1
2026-03-17T09:12:22Z runtime-ppool-3 WARN kvcache lock wait > 1200ms
2026-03-17T09:12:24Z runtime-ppool-3 ERR upstream write failed: broken pipe
2026-03-17T09:12:24Z gateway gw01 504 responding to client"

Ben (Devex): Note: our older JS SDK (<=1.1.x) will aggressively retry streaming on socket errors. That combination can create retry storms when the proxy returns 504. Recommend asking the customer to upgrade to SDK v1.3.2 which includes streaming backoff and idempotency guards. Also suggest setting maxRetries=2 temporarily.

Maya (Support): Customer says they're on SDK 1.1.7 right now and can't upgrade immediately. They asked if we can provide a server-side mitigation.

Sam (SRE): Short-term: we can relax the gateway streaming keepalive from 60s -> 90s for the Videx tenant or route them to a less-loaded gateway to reduce connection churn. I'll test on a staging route.

Leo (Eng-runtime): Longer-term: those kvcache lock waits are worrying. Could be KV cache thrash when many concurrent streams hit large context lengths. Can you confirm payload sizes?

Maya (Support): Customer: average prompt ~20k tokens, some ops 80k token priming. They admitted some large requests hit at the same time.

Ben (Devex): That explains it — large contexts + streaming + old SDK retries = higher probability of interleaved connection resets. If we can get them routed to dedicated pool with higher kvcache capacity that should help.

ci-bot: Deploy note: rolled edge config update edge-keepalive-tune -> gw01 at 2026-03-17T09:05:12Z (change id cfg_1379).

Sam (SRE): Hmm cfg_1379 matches timeframe. Rolling back that config on gw01 to see if it correlates with the spike. Will post results in ~10m.

Anya (Customer Success): I'll notify Videx that we're investigating and ask them to hold rollback/upgrade until we have a short mitigation ready. Proposed message: "We're seeing a transient edge issue impacting streaming in us-west; engineers are testing a config rollback and we will update in 15 minutes." OK?

Maya (Support): Fine. Please include suggestion to set SDK maxRetries=0 as a temporary client patch if they can.

Leo (Eng-runtime): Can someone drop a small repro script we can run against staging that mimics their large streaming + retry behavior? I can try to reproduce kvcache lock and correlation with cfg_1379.

Maya (Support): Pasting quick Node repro (sanitized):
```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RWD_KEY});
async function run() {
  for (let i=0; i<12; i++) {
    client.generateStream({model:'rwd-stream-2', input: 'x'.repeat(50000)})
      .on('data', d=>console.log(i, 'chunk'))
      .on('error', e=> console.log('err', e.code));
  }
}
run();
```

Ben (Devex): Good — I'll run that against staging with SDK v1.1.7 and v1.3.2 to quantify difference.

Sam (SRE): Rolling back cfg_1379 on gw01 now. If the 504 spike drops in the next 5-10 minutes we'll consider that a blocker for the change.

(10m pass)

Sam (SRE): Update: after rollback gw01 504 rate for Videx dropped from ~18/min -> ~2/min. Still seeing a few 504s correlated with the largest payloads (~80k token requests).

Leo (Eng-runtime): That's a helpful signal — edge config change increased sensitivity to upstream write/backpressure. We'll schedule a follow-up to tune keepalive and runtime kvcache resizing. For now mitigation options: route Videx to dedicated pool, increase gateway keepalive, or encourage SDK patch.

Anya (Customer Success): Draft message for Videx: "We've rolled back a recent edge change which reduced the error rate. For full mitigation we recommend either upgrading your SDK to v1.3.2 (best) or enabling client-side maxRetries=0 while we provision a dedicated pool. We're happy to coordinate a maintenance window."

Maya (Support): I'll send that note. Marking this thread as ongoing; will escalate to runtime eng for kvcache sizing ticket and to infra for a dedicated pool quote. Continuing updates here.

Sam (SRE): Filed incident ticket INC-2026-0317-videx (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0317). Assigning to Leo for runtime follow-up.

Leo (Eng-runtime): Acknowledged. I'll take the runtime side and post perf traces after I run the Node repro.

Maya (Support): Thanks all — customer call scheduled in 30m. I'll update thread after call.

Maya (Support): (post-call) Videx accepted temporary client change (maxRetries=0) and confirmed error rate dropped to near zero. They're willing to plan an SDK upgrade next week. Closing customer-facing urgent phase; leaving infra/eng follow-ups open.
